Alternatively, passive tension refers to when a two-joint muscle is elongated at one joint while carrying out dynamic movement at the other joint. This produces a favorable length-tension relationship, enhancing the muscle's ability to produce force. For example, the long head of the triceps brachii crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, carrying out shoulder flexion and elbow extension at these joints, respectively. Because the muscle is shortened during shoulder exten- sion, it is lengthened during shoulder flexion.
